blocks.text: The standard library's `sort.sort_by` sorts a list with a "comes before" rule that you give. You write the rule as a lambda: return `true` if `a` should come before `b`.

code: sort.sort_by(v, fn(a: i32, b: i32) -> bool => a > b)

blocks.prompt: Change the lambda to sort the same list from **smallest to biggest**.
starter: sort.sort_by(v, fn(a: i32, b: i32) -> bool => a > b)
solution: sort.sort_by(v, fn(a: i32, b: i32) -> bool => a < b)

blocks.q: What does it mean when the lambda given to `sort_by` returns `true`?
blocks.why: The lambda answers the question "comes before?".
